text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - A mid-afternoon report showing stronger-than- expected jobs growth in the U.S. in December sent German Bunds into negative territory in late dealings, dashing earlier hopes for an end-of-week rally. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.04, down 0.23 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts closed unchanged as early gains on weak domestic data melted away after a stronger than expected rise in US non-farm payrolls. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-30/32, down 1/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures finished MATIF trading weaker, but suffered less than other debt markets after the publication of strong U.S. job creation figures, buffered by continuing hopes of further interest rate reduction in France. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.70, down 0.06 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets remained in positive territory on the last day of the week despite falls in U.S. and German bond markets. The March bond future on LIFFE was at 128.85, up 0.12 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - Renewed fears of a near-term tightening by the Federal Reserve sent U.S. Treasury prices tumbling and yields soaring to levels not seen in more than three months. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-1/32, down 1-12/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.88 percent.

JAPAN - Key March Japanese government bond futures rose sharply toward the close, as Tokyo share prices nosedived in the afternoon. Traders said the sharp fall in share prices led to the view that current low interest rates would remain unchanged for the time being, and was supportive of JGBs. In after-hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 125.46, up 0.51 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Peripheral currencies dominated Eurobond activity, with most issued targeted at retail investors. Three Czech crown deals for a total of 3.5 billion crowns surfaced, reflecting strong demand for its high yields. Westdeutsche Landesbank brought a 200 million rand three-year bond and Eurofima followed with a 150 million rand one-year issue. Dollar deals were absent ahead of December U.S. non-farm payroll data but a number of jumbo issues were expected to surface next week.
